chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The fruit juice does not become impure (haram) until it boils."

key_terms.الْعَصِيرُ: Fruit juice, specifically the juice of grapes or other fruits pressed without added water.
key_terms.يَحْرُمُ: Becomes forbidden/impure; in this context, refers to the state of najasah (ritual impurity) or change in legal status.
key_terms.يَغْلِيَ: Boils; refers to the physical state of the liquid reaching its boiling point, indicating fermentation or change.

ai.seo_question: When does fruit juice become impure in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of Shia fiqh, this hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the status of grape juice ('asir) regarding its transition from pure to impure or intoxicating. It establishes that mere standing or initial fermentation does not render it najis; rather, the critical threshold for prohibition or change in status is reached only when the liquid boils (ghalayn), a key criterion in distinguishing between mild fermentation and full intoxication.
